subject.name: Physics
subject.description: Cambridge IGCSE Physics. Core students take Papers 1 and 3; Extended students take Papers 2 and 4. Momentum (1.6) is Extended content only. Calculations use g = 9.8 N/kg, and you can type answers in standard form, for example 3.0e8. The practical papers (5 and 6) are not included. The questions are original practice questions written in the style of Cambridge papers, not reproduced past paper material.

topics.title: Physical quantities and measurement techniques
topics.summary: Measuring length, volume and time; scalars and vectors.

topics.title: Motion
topics.summary: Speed, velocity, acceleration, distance–time and speed–time graphs.

topics.title: Mass and weight
topics.summary: Mass, weight and gravitational field strength.

topics.title: Density
topics.summary: Calculating and measuring density; floating and sinking.

topics.title: Forces
topics.summary: Effects of forces, turning effect, centre of gravity.

topics.title: Momentum
topics.summary: Momentum, impulse and conservation of momentum (Extended).

topics.title: Energy, work and power
topics.summary: Energy stores and transfers, work, power, energy resources.

topics.title: Pressure
topics.summary: Pressure on surfaces and in liquids.

topics.title: Kinetic particle model of matter
topics.summary: States of matter, particle model, gases and pressure.

topics.title: Thermal properties and temperature
topics.summary: Thermal expansion, specific heat capacity, melting, boiling and evaporation.

topics.title: Transfer of thermal energy
topics.summary: Conduction, convection and radiation.

topics.title: General properties of waves
topics.summary: Wave motion, transverse and longitudinal waves, reflection, refraction, diffraction.

topics.title: Light
topics.summary: Reflection, refraction, thin lenses, dispersion.

topics.title: Electromagnetic spectrum
topics.summary: Regions, uses and dangers of electromagnetic waves.

topics.title: Sound
topics.summary: Production, speed and reflection of sound; ultrasound.

topics.title: Simple phenomena of magnetism
topics.summary: Magnets, magnetic fields and materials.

topics.title: Electrical quantities
topics.summary: Charge, current, e.m.f., potential difference, resistance, energy and power.

topics.title: Electric circuits
topics.summary: Series and parallel circuits, potential dividers.

topics.title: Electrical safety
topics.summary: Hazards, fuses, circuit breakers and earthing.

topics.title: Electromagnetic effects
topics.summary: Induction, the a.c. generator, motors, transformers.

topics.title: The nuclear model of the atom
topics.summary: Atomic structure, nuclide notation, the nucleus.

topics.title: Radioactivity
topics.summary: Detection, types of emission, decay, half-life, safety.

topics.title: Earth and the Solar System
topics.summary: The Earth, the Moon, the Sun and planets, orbits.

topics.title: Stars and the Universe
topics.summary: The Sun as a star, stellar life cycles, the Universe and the Big Bang.

parts.prompt: Which quantity is a vector?
parts.examinerComment: Velocity has direction; speed does not.

parts.prompt: A car travels 150 m in 10 s. What is its average speed?
What is the weight of a 5.0 kg mass on Earth? (g = 9.8 N/kg)
A block has a mass of 200 g and a volume of 25 cm³. What is its density?
A spring extends by 2.0 cm for each 1.0 N of load, within its limit of proportionality. What is its extension with a 3.0 N load?
parts.examinerComment: The extension is proportional to the load.

parts.prompt: In which energy store is energy kept in a stretched spring?
A force of 600 N acts on an area of 0.20 m². What is the pressure?
What causes the pressure of a gas on the walls of its container?

markingPoints.text: A – particles colliding with the walls

parts.prompt: Why are small gaps left between sections of railway track?

markingPoints.text: A – to allow for thermal expansion

parts.prompt: Which process can transfer thermal energy through a vacuum?
A wave has a frequency of 5.0 Hz and a wavelength of 2.0 m. What is its speed?
Light strikes a plane mirror with an angle of incidence of 30°. What is the angle of reflection?
parts.examinerComment: Angles are measured from the normal.

parts.prompt: Which part of the electromagnetic spectrum has the longest wavelength?
What is the approximate range of human hearing?
Two magnets are placed with their north poles facing each other. What happens?
How is an ammeter connected to measure the current through a lamp?

markingPoints.text: B – in series with the lamp

parts.prompt: A 2.0 Ω resistor and a 4.0 Ω resistor are connected in series. What is the combined resistance?
What is the purpose of a fuse in a plug?

options.text: to melt and break the circuit if the current is too high

markingPoints.text: C – to melt and break the circuit if the current is too high

parts.prompt: A magnet is pushed into a coil connected to a meter. Which change increases the induced e.m.f.?
What does the nucleus of an atom contain?
Which type of radiation is the most strongly ionising?
parts.examinerComment: Alpha is the most ionising and the least penetrating.

parts.prompt: How long does the Earth take to orbit the Sun?
Which statement about the Sun is correct?

options.text: It is a medium-sized star made mostly of hydrogen and helium.
It is the largest star in the Universe.
It produces energy by burning coal.

markingPoints.text: B – It is a medium-sized star made mostly of hydrogen and helium.

parts.prompt: What is the momentum of a 2.0 kg trolley moving at 3.0 m/s?
A stack of 50 sheets of paper is 4.0 mm thick. Calculate the thickness of one sheet, in mm.
parts.examinerComment: Measuring many sheets and dividing reduces the uncertainty.

parts.prompt: A cyclist accelerates from rest to 20 m/s in 8.0 s. Calculate the acceleration, in m/s².
State two differences between mass and weight.

markingPoints.text: mass is the quantity of matter; weight is a gravitational force
mass is measured in kg; weight in N
weight changes with gravitational field strength; mass does not

parts.examinerComment: Many candidates gave units only. Defining each quantity earns more credit.

parts.prompt: Describe how to find the density of an irregularly shaped stone.

markingPoints.text: measure the mass using a balance
find the volume by displacement: the rise in water level in a measuring cylinder

parts.examinerComment: Answers should name the measuring instruments.

parts.prompt: A force of 20 N acts 0.30 m from a pivot. Calculate its moment, in N m.

markingPoints.text: C1 for moment = force × perpendicular distance

parts.prompt: A crate of weight 50 N is lifted through a height of 2.0 m. Calculate the work done, in J.
Explain why tractors used on soft ground have wide tyres.

markingPoints.text: wide tyres give a larger area
so the pressure on the ground is smaller and the tractor sinks less

parts.examinerComment: Answers must link area to pressure.

parts.prompt: Describe the motion of particles in a gas.

markingPoints.text: at high speed, in straight lines between collisions

parts.prompt: Name the process in which a liquid changes to a gas at its surface, at a temperature below its boiling point.
parts.examinerComment: Boiling happens throughout the liquid at its boiling point.

parts.prompt: Explain why a metal spoon in a cup of hot tea quickly feels hot.

markingPoints.text: thermal energy is transferred by conduction
metals are good conductors because they have free (delocalised) electrons

parts.prompt: Define the wavelength of a wave.

markingPoints.text: the distance between two adjacent crests (or corresponding points)

parts.prompt: State two characteristics of the image formed by a plane mirror.

markingPoints.text: same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front

parts.prompt: Give one use of microwaves.
A student claps near a cliff and hears the echo 0.40 s later. The speed of sound is 340 m/s. Calculate the distance to the cliff, in m.

markingPoints.text: C1 for halving: the sound travels there and back

parts.examinerComment: Many forgot that the sound travels to the cliff and back.

parts.prompt: Name a magnetic material.
parts.examinerComment: Aluminium and copper are not magnetic.

parts.prompt: The potential difference across a resistor is 12 V and the current is 0.50 A. Calculate its resistance, in Ω.
Two 10 Ω resistors are connected in series to a 6.0 V battery. Calculate the current, in A.
Explain why the earth wire is connected to the metal case of an appliance.

markingPoints.text: if a live wire touches the case, current flows to earth
the large current melts the fuse, so the case does not stay live and the user is not electrocuted

parts.examinerComment: Good answers linked the earth wire to the fuse.

parts.prompt: State one way to increase the force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field.

markingPoints.text: increase the current / use a stronger magnet

parts.prompt: A nuclide of uranium is ²³⁸₉₂U. How many neutrons does its nucleus contain?
A radioactive sample has a half-life of 6.0 hours. Its count rate is 800 counts/minute. Calculate the count rate after 18 hours, in counts/minute.
Explain why the Earth has day and night.

markingPoints.text: the Earth rotates on its axis
once every 24 hours, so each side faces towards and then away from the Sun

parts.examinerComment: Some said the Earth orbits the Sun once a day.

parts.prompt: What does a light-year measure?

markingPoints.text: distance (the distance light travels in one year)

parts.examinerComment: It is not a unit of time.

figures.alt: Circuit diagram: a 12 V cell in series with a 4.0 Ω resistor, a 2.0 Ω resistor and an ammeter.
figures.caption: Fig. 1

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the reading on the ammeter, in A.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the potential difference across the 4.0 Ω resistor, in V.
parts.examinerComment: The p.d.s across the resistors add up to the supply voltage.

questions.stem: Fig. 2 shows the speed–time graph for a cyclist.

figures.alt: Speed–time graph: speed rises steadily from 0 to 10 m/s in 4 s, stays at 10 m/s until 10 s, then falls to 0 at 12 s.
figures.caption: Fig. 2

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Describe the motion of the cyclist between 4 s and 10 s.
parts.examinerComment: 'Not moving' was a common misreading of a horizontal line.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total distance travelled by the cyclist, in m.

markingPoints.text: C1 for area under the graph

parts.examinerComment: Splitting the area into triangles and a rectangle helps.

questions.stem: Fig. 4 shows how the count rate from a radioactive source changes with time. The background count has been subtracted.

figures.alt: Graph of count rate against time: the count rate falls from 800 counts per minute at 0 hours, halving every 2 hours.
figures.caption: Fig. 4

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use Fig. 4 to find the half-life of the source, in hours.

markingPoints.text: C1 for reading the time for 800 to fall to 400

parts.examinerComment: Draw lines on the graph to show your reading.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the count rate after 4.0 hours, in counts per minute.
Forces of 3.0 N east and 4.0 N north act on an object. Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force, in N.
parts.examinerComment: Forces at right angles are added using Pythagoras' theorem, not by adding.

parts.prompt: A train accelerates uniformly from rest to 12 m/s in 6.0 s. Calculate the distance travelled in this time, in m.

markingPoints.text: C1 for area under the speed–time graph: ½ × 6.0 × 12

parts.examinerComment: Multiplying final speed by time gives twice the correct answer.

parts.prompt: An astronaut has a mass of 70 kg. The gravitational field strength on the Moon is 1.6 N/kg. Calculate the astronaut's weight on the Moon, in N.
parts.examinerComment: The astronaut's mass does not change.

parts.prompt: An object of density 0.90 g/cm³ is placed in water of density 1.0 g/cm³. State and explain whether it floats or sinks.

markingPoints.text: because its density is less than that of water

parts.prompt: Calculate the resultant force needed to give a car of mass 1200 kg an acceleration of 2.5 m/s², in N.
A force of 400 N acts on a ball for 0.050 s. Calculate the impulse, in N s.
A 2.0 kg trolley moving at 3.0 m/s collides with a stationary 1.0 kg trolley and they stick together. Calculate their speed after the collision, in m/s.

markingPoints.text: C1 for momentum before = 6.0 kg m/s

parts.examinerComment: Momentum is conserved; kinetic energy is not.

parts.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy of a 0.50 kg ball moving at 8.0 m/s, in J.
parts.examinerComment: Squaring only the speed, not the product mv, was essential.

parts.prompt: Calculate the change in pressure at a depth of 5.0 m in water of density 1000 kg/m³, in Pa. (g = 9.8 N/kg)
A fixed mass of gas at constant temperature has a pressure of 100 kPa and a volume of 2.0 m³. It is compressed to 0.50 m³. Calculate the new pressure, in kPa.
Calculate the energy needed to raise the temperature of 2.0 kg of water by 15 °C, in J. (specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J/(kg °C))
Water in a pan is heated from below. Explain how a convection current forms.

markingPoints.text: water near the heat source expands
cooler, denser water sinks to take its place

parts.examinerComment: 'Heat rises' is not acceptable. It is the less dense water that rises.

parts.prompt: Water waves travel from deep water into shallow water. State what happens to their speed, wavelength and frequency.
parts.examinerComment: Frequency is set by the source and does not change.

parts.prompt: A ray of light passes from air into glass. The angle of incidence is 40° and the angle of refraction is 25°. Calculate the refractive index of the glass, to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: C1 for n = sin i ÷ sin r

parts.examinerComment: Calculators must be in degree mode.

parts.prompt: State the speed of electromagnetic waves in a vacuum, in m/s.
parts.examinerComment: Answers can be typed as 3.0e8 or 3.0 × 10^8.

parts.prompt: Explain why sound cannot travel through a vacuum.

markingPoints.text: because it travels as vibrations of particles (a longitudinal wave)

parts.prompt: Describe how to plot the magnetic field lines around a bar magnet using a plotting compass.

markingPoints.text: place the compass near one pole and mark the direction the needle points
move the compass so its tail is at the last mark and repeat
join the dots to form a line, from N to S, and repeat from other starting points

parts.prompt: A current of 0.25 A flows for 2.0 minutes. Calculate the charge that passes, in C.

markingPoints.text: C1 for Q = It with t = 120 s

parts.examinerComment: Minutes must be converted to seconds.

parts.prompt: Calculate the combined resistance of a 6.0 Ω resistor and a 3.0 Ω resistor connected in parallel, in Ω.
parts.examinerComment: The combined resistance must be less than the smallest resistor.

parts.prompt: A kettle is rated at 2300 W, 230 V. Calculate the current and choose a suitable fuse from 3 A, 5 A and 13 A.

markingPoints.text: 13 A fuse (the next value above the normal current)

parts.prompt: A transformer has 2000 turns on its primary coil and 100 turns on its secondary coil. The primary voltage is 230 V. Calculate the secondary voltage, in V.
Describe what the alpha-particle scattering experiment showed about the structure of the atom.

markingPoints.text: most alpha particles passed straight through, so the atom is mostly empty space
a few were deflected through large angles
so the nucleus is very small, dense and positively charged

parts.prompt: Radium-226 (²²⁶₈₈Ra) decays by alpha emission to radon (Rn). Write the nuclide equation.

markingPoints.text: nucleon and proton numbers balance on both sides

parts.prompt: The Earth orbits the Sun at an average radius of 1.5 × 10¹¹ m with a period of 3.2 × 10⁷ s. Calculate its average orbital speed, in m/s.
The Hubble constant is about 2.2 × 10⁻¹⁸ s⁻¹. Estimate the age of the Universe, in s, using 1 ÷ H₀.

questions.stem: Fig. 2 shows the speed–time graph for a cyclist.

figures.alt: Speed–time graph: speed rises steadily from 0 to 10 m/s in 4 s, stays at 10 m/s until 10 s, then falls to 0 at 12 s.
figures.caption: Fig. 2

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the acceleration of the cyclist during the first 4 s, in m/s².

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the deceleration of the cyclist between 10 s and 12 s, in m/s².
parts.examinerComment: Give the deceleration as a positive value.

figures.alt: Circuit diagram: a 6.0 V cell with an ammeter in the main circuit, connected to a 3.0 Ω resistor and a 6.0 Ω resistor in parallel.
figures.caption: Fig. 3

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the current in the 3.0 Ω resistor, in A.

markingPoints.text: C1 for the p.d. across each branch is 6.0 V

parts.examinerComment: Each parallel branch has the full supply voltage.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the reading on the ammeter, in A.
parts.examinerComment: The current in the main circuit is the sum of the branch currents.
